editorial:
Imagine waking up in 1937 and getting a job where one wrong word could get you killed. You follow a new prosecutor who thinks he can actually do the right thing during Stalin's Great Terror. He finds out that the Secret Police are corrupt and decides to play detective to uncover the truth. The vibe is very tense and heavy, making you feel like someone is always watching over your shoulder. It feels less like a history lesson and more like a dangerous game of cat and mouse where the stakes are life and death.

The acting is top-notch, especially the way the lead actor shows fear without saying a word. While the pacing starts a bit slow, the tension builds up until you can barely breathe. If you like mysteries that make you think, you will love this.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a cruel twist. After the prosecutor gathers all the evidence against the corrupt police officers, he realizes he was just a pawn in a bigger game. His bosses wanted the police cleaned out, but they didn't want the evidence to go public. Instead of being a hero, he is arrested and framed for the very crimes he uncovered. He ends up in the same prison he helped fill, showing that no one is safe.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves political thrillers and historical mysteries.
